study.title: I give You thanks with all my heart
study.intro: Psalm 138 begins a final group of eight psalms of David (138-145). It is a wholehearted thank-you for answered prayer. David praises God's loving devotion and faithfulness, remembers the day God answered and strengthened him, and imagines the kings of the earth joining in praise. Though God is exalted, He cares for the lowly, and David trusts that God will complete His purpose for his life.
study.context: Headed 'of David', this psalm thanks God for a specific answered prayer, likely connected to God's promises to David's house (2 Samuel 7). David sings 'before the gods', boldly praising the LORD in a world full of other gods and the powers behind them. Its closing line, 'do not abandon the works of Your hands', is a humble plea that God will finish what He has started.
study.peopleNote: Attributed to David. Kings of the earth are pictured joining in praise. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Wholehearted thanks
verses.heading: Singing before the gods
verses.meaning: 'I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises.' David holds nothing back. His thanks comes from his whole heart, not just his lips. And he sings 'before the gods,' boldly praising the LORD in front of every rival power. In a world full of competing loyalties, he declares where his gratitude belongs.
verses.context: Psalm 9:1 also says, 'I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart.' Daniel and his friends refused to bow to other gods (Daniel 3:18). Psalm 96:4-5 says all the gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
explore: With all my heart
Wholeheartedly, with the whole inner self engaged, not half-hearted or distracted.
Before the gods
In the presence of rival powers and false gods, as a bold public witness.
verses.reflect: What would wholehearted thanks to God look like for you today?
verses.alt: A man playing a lyre on a hillside with arms lifted toward the sky.

verses.title: Bowing toward the temple
verses.heading: Your name and Your word above all else
verses.meaning: 'I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness; You have exalted Your name and Your word above all else.' David bows toward God's dwelling. He thanks God for two things: loving devotion and faithfulness. God has shown that His promise, His word, is as great as His name. When God speaks, He keeps it.
verses.context: 2 Samuel 7:28 has David saying, 'Your words are true, and You have promised this good thing.' Daniel prayed toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10). Isaiah 55:11 says God's word will not return empty.
explore: Holy temple
God's dwelling place, set apart for His worship and presence.
Faithfulness
God's reliability and trustworthiness; He always keeps His promises.
verses.reflect: What promise of God have you seen Him keep in your own life?
verses.alt: A worshiper kneeling on a mat facing toward a distant temple at dawn.

verses.title: Answered and strengthened
verses.heading: You emboldened me
verses.meaning: 'On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.' David remembers a specific day. He prayed, and God answered. The answer may not have removed every problem, but it did something just as important: it made him bold and strong inside. Sometimes God's answer is not a change of circumstances but new courage to face them.
verses.context: Isaiah 40:29 says God gives strength to the weary. Ephesians 3:16 prays that believers be strengthened with power through His Spirit in the inner being. Acts 4:29-31 tells of early believers praying for boldness and receiving it.
explore: Emboldened
Made bold and confident, given courage to act without fear.
Soul
The inner self, the whole person's life, desires and heart.
verses.reflect: When has God answered your prayer with courage rather than an immediate change?
verses.alt: A traveler standing tall on a windy ridge with the path ahead in view.

verses.title: Kings will give thanks
verses.heading: When they hear the words of Your mouth
verses.meaning: 'All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth.' David's personal thanks widens to a vision for the world. One day the rulers of every nation will hear God's word and thank Him too. God's promises to one man are part of a plan to reach the nations. The New Testament sees this coming true as the gospel spreads.
verses.context: Psalm 72:11 says all kings will bow down before the Messiah. Isaiah 60:3 says kings will come to the brightness of God's rising. Revelation 21:24 says the kings of the earth will bring their glory into the new Jerusalem.
explore: Kings of the earth
Rulers of all the nations, representing the whole world.
Words of Your mouth
What God has spoken, His promises and revealed word.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God's word will reach the whole world encourage you?
verses.alt: Rulers in varied robes arriving at a city gate from different roads.

verses.title: Singing of His ways
verses.heading: The glory of the LORD is great
verses.meaning: 'They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.' The kings will not only thank God but sing about His ways, how He acts in the world. His glory, His weight and splendor, is great beyond all earthly glory. When rulers who once loved their own greatness sing about God's, it is a sign that His glory has truly been seen.
verses.context: Exodus 33:13 has Moses praying, 'Show me Your ways.' Isaiah 6:3 says the whole earth is full of His glory. Habakkuk 2:14 says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.
explore: Ways
God's actions and character, how He deals with the world and with people.
Glory
God's weight, splendor and honor, the shining of who He is.
verses.reflect: Which of God's ways would you sing about if you wrote a song today?
verses.alt: A sunrise spreading golden light over a wide land.

verses.title: High yet near the lowly
verses.heading: He attends to the lowly
verses.meaning: 'Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly; but the proud He knows from afar.' Here is a beautiful paradox. God is exalted above everything, yet He bends down to care for the humble. The proud, meanwhile, He keeps at a distance. Greatness in God's kingdom means humility. The lowly are not overlooked; they are the ones God draws near to.
verses.context: Isaiah 57:15 says God dwells in a high and holy place, and also with the contrite and lowly in spirit. James 4:6 says God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. Luke 1:52 says He lifted up the humble.
explore: Lowly
Humble, poor or of low status; those who know their need of God.
From afar
At a distance; God sees the proud clearly but does not draw close to them.
verses.reflect: How does it encourage you that God draws near to the lowly?
verses.alt: A shepherd boy sitting on a rock with sheep under a vast sky.

verses.title: Preserved in trouble
verses.heading: Your right hand saves me
verses.meaning: 'If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me from the anger of my foes; You extend Your hand, and Your right hand saves me.' David does not expect a trouble-free life. He expects to walk right through the middle of hard things. But he trusts that God will keep him alive and reach out His strong hand to save. God's help meets us in the trouble, not only after it.
verses.context: Psalm 23:4 says, 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil.' Isaiah 41:10 says God will uphold you with His righteous right hand. John 16:33 says in the world you will have trouble, but Jesus has overcome it.
explore: Preserve
To keep alive and safe, protecting from destruction.
Right hand
A picture of God's strength and power to act and save.
verses.reflect: What trouble are you walking through? How might God be preserving you in it?
verses.alt: A figure walking through a narrow gorge with light ahead.

verses.title: He will fulfill His purpose
verses.heading: Do not abandon the works of Your hands
verses.meaning: 'The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever—do not abandon the works of Your hands.' David ends with confidence and a humble request. God will finish what He has planned for him. His love lasts forever. And yet David still prays, 'Don't let go of what You have made.' Faith trusts God's promise and keeps praying for it at the same time.
verses.context: Philippians 1:6 says He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion. Isaiah 64:8 says we are the clay and You are the potter; we are the work of Your hand. Romans 8:28 says God works all things together for good.
explore: Fulfill
To complete or carry out fully, bringing something to its intended end.
Works of Your hands
What God has made; here David himself and God's people, His creation.
verses.reflect: What do you trust God to finish in your life? Pray for it with confidence.
verses.alt: A potter's wheel with a half-finished clay jar in soft workshop light.
